archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate attacker)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower whose value comes almost entirely from attempts beyond 10 air yards, especially between the numbers. He adds a little as a scrambler but is not a designed-run threat.

report.headline: Accurate at last: McCarthy's downfield rebuild is real, but sacks and red zone lag
report.take:
McCarthy arrives in New York as a very different passer from the one the 2025 Vikings tape showed. That version completed 57.6% with a -5.7 CPOE, threw 12 interceptions and graded 50th of 63 in EPA per play. Three starts into his Giants run (W7-W10), the accuracy profile has flipped. His CPOE is up 9.3 points on last year, his bad-throw rate is down 4.7 points and he is getting the ball out about a quarter-second faster. A 8.8 yards per attempt that ranks 5th of 54 is not a game-manager line. He is playing in a run-leaning Harbaugh offense that passes 5.1 points below expectation, yet the dropbacks he does get are productive.

The engine is one band of the field. On throws of 10+ air yards he is at +0.679 EPA per attempt and 53.5% success, adding 29.2 EPA total. Under 10 air yards he is below water at -0.102, and screens and swings behind the line are a drag at -0.275. Throws to the middle (87.5% completions, +19.2 CPOE) carry the profile, and Isaiah Likely's +0.492 EPA per target is the clearest sign of where his eyes go. Malik Nabers leads the targets but returns far less per look. That points to a quarterback reading seams and in-breakers, not one feeding his best receiver.

The numbers hide two drags, one structural and one probably noise. The structural one is sacks. His pressure-to-sack rate of 43.5% is 40th of 42, and last year's 0.351 ranked 39th of 62, so this is who he is, not a new problem. He holds the ball looking for the intermediate window. Behind a line that ranks 29th in hit rate allowed, that habit produced a five-sack, -2.2 EPA day at Philadelphia. The noise is touchdowns. A 1.9% TD rate (45th) and a 9-play red-zone sample at -0.898 EPA are far too thin to define him. A passer this efficient between the 20s should not keep finishing drives this poorly.

Where it's heading: the accuracy gains look real enough to bet on, because they show up across depths and in his charting, not just in a couple of big games. But he is on 27.7 attempts a game in a run-first system, so the ceiling is volume-capped. His weekly floor depends on whether the protection lets him get to the throws that carry his value.

strengths.title: Lives in the 10-plus air-yard band
strengths.body: Nearly all of his passing value comes on throws of 10+ air yards, where he is efficient and accurate rather than just aggressive. This reflects how he plays: he reads the second level and throws on time. That gives it a better chance of holding than a few lucky shots. The deep CPOE will cool on 19 attempts, but the intermediate production is the steadier base.

strengths.title: Accuracy turnaround from 2025
strengths.body: His completion percentage over expected swung from well below average last year to comfortably above it. His bad-throw rate also fell sharply. Faster processing (time to throw down 0.26 seconds) is the likely cause, and a mechanical or processing change like that tends to stick better than a hot streak. It is still only three starts' worth of evidence.

strengths.title: Middle of the field, Likely
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers are his best area by a wide margin, and the tight end is the main beneficiary. That pairing gives the offense a dependable chain-mover even with the run-first lean.

concerns.title: Sacks are a career-long habit
concerns.body: He turns pressure into sacks at one of the worst rates in the league. Last year's rank was nearly identical, so this is a trait, not a blip. Holding the ball for intermediate windows is the price of his best throws, and a line ranked 29th in hit rate makes the bill steeper. Expect this to persist, along with the occasional drive-killing game like Philadelphia.

concerns.title: Red-zone and TD output lag
concerns.body: His touchdown rate sits near the bottom of qualifiers, and his red-zone work has been ugly. Both rest on tiny samples, and his efficiency elsewhere argues they rise toward normal. Even so, a run-leaning offense will take some goal-to-go chances out of his hands.

concerns.title: Short game and right side
concerns.body: Under 10 air yards he loses value, and throws to the right side have been negative with both interceptions. Some of that is noise on modest samples. Still, it means his efficiency depends on getting the defense to give him intermediate looks.

trend.note: His three starts went +5.1 passing EPA at Houston, -2.2 with five sacks at Philadelphia, then +5.2 with a season-high 293 yards against Washington. The swings track the protection more than his accuracy, which held up in all three.

nextGame.headline: Jacksonville smothers the short game but bleeds deep: his lane
nextGame.body:
Jacksonville is a top-five defense overall and against the pass. Its shape fits McCarthy's profile oddly well. It is the stingiest unit in the league on short throws, which is the part of his game he gets little from anyway. It is 28th against deep passes, where he has done his best work. It also leans hard against the run, so offenses pass on it more than usual. As a six-point home underdog facing a top-four offense, the Giants may be pushed off their run-first script. That could mean more dropbacks than his recent 27.7 a game. The catch is his preferred targets. Jacksonville has held lead receivers and especially top tight ends well below their norms, so the Likely seam work may be harder to find.

Availability is clean on his side: no Giants offensive players on the report, a full practice and ten days of rest after the Thursday game. Jacksonville's listed injuries mostly touch its offense (center Robert Hainsey's knee) or its depth. Danny Striggow is a 25%-snap end in concussion evaluation, and B.J. Green II hasn't played. Neither changes the pass rush McCarthy will see much. That rush rarely finishes with sacks, a modest break for a quarterback who takes too many.

keyMatchups.title: His deep ball vs their leak
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville allows heavy EPA on deep throws while choking everything short. McCarthy's value is concentrated beyond 10 air yards. If he gets time, this is the single most favorable alignment in the game.

keyMatchups.title: Likely against a TE-proof defense
keyMatchups.body: His most productive target meets the defense that has been stingiest against top tight ends. If the middle-field seam is taken away, he has to win to his receivers. Some of his read-based efficiency rides on that seam.

keyMatchups.title: Pass-funnel game script
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville's run defense pushes opponents to throw, and the spread suggests the Giants trail. A low sack rate on their side gives him a cleaner chance to hold for intermediate windows than Philadelphia allowed.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Giants let him throw 30-plus times. Watch especially how many of those go beyond 10 air yards against a defense that concedes deep and nothing short.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy and intermediate efficiency look like a real step forward rather than a three-game fluke. They show up in his charting, his depth splits and his processing speed, and none of it was present in 2025. What caps him is the system and the line. The Giants pass well below expectation, and his sack habit has followed him across teams. Expect efficient but modest volume, around 195-250 passing yards a game. Yardage can climb when game script forces passing, and an occasional floor game will come when pressure gets home.

The touchdown drought is where the regression should come. A passer this productive between the 20s should find the end zone closer to once a game, though a run-first red-zone plan limits it. The 17-game pace figures blend in two relief appearances and aren't a useful guide. His rushing stays a small, scramble-driven bonus: designed runs have been stuffed often, while his scrambles pay off.
swingFactors: Pass protection and his pressure-to-sack habit
Whether Harbaugh opens up the pass rate

confidence.note: Three starts and 104 attempts, a sharp break from his 2025 profile, and a new team and system.
